title: Consolidate GPU linkage sandbox and symtab demultiplexer to reduce cold-start jitter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Reduce runtime startup jitter and inter-node variance caused by ad-hoc shared-object probing and symbol resolution across heterogeneous GPU images. This ticket refactors the current probe + lazy-linking behavior into a small, deterministic 'linkage sandbox' that performs staged isolation of CUTLASS/Triton bindings and a symbol demultiplexer (symtab-demux) that only exposes a minimal stable ABI surface to the runtime hotpath. The goal is to remove nondeterministic ld.so order-dependent behavior, reduce cold-start wall time by >=20%, and provide a testable compatibility boundary for future CUTLASS/Triton upgrades.
background: Over the past year we've accumulated many point-fixes to handle symbol collisions, ABI mismatches, and opportunistic prelinking. Those fixes reduce immediate incidents but increase complexity: multiple probe paths, per-arch fallback heuristics, and on-demand jitting of symbol stubs. This manifests as warmup variance across pods and occasional OOMs when fallbacks trigger late. Prior tickets (ENG-271450, ENG-317215, ENG-428001) cleaned parts of the stack but did not centralize a deterministic linkage layer. This work consolidates those improvements into a single predictable initialization flow.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce 'linkage-sandbox' binary component that preloads and validates kernel bundles in a sandboxed namespace before the main runtime initializes
Implement symtab-demux that maps only the documented runtime ABI to the main process and rejects unknown symbol versions
Reduce 95th-percentile cold-start latency for model-serving containers by at least 20% in our mixed-GPU canary cluster
Add unit and integration tests that simulate mismatched CUTLASS/Triton variants and assert graceful fallback without triggering late-symbol-loads
Document the new compatibility contract and migration notes for on-call and partner engineering
implementation_plan: Design: define the minimal exported symbol set required by the runtime and create symtab contract doc
Prototype: build a small orchestrator that spawns the sandboxed prelink process and reports verified bundles via FD-passing
Integrate: replace opportunistic probe codepaths with calls to the sandbox verifier and allow a deterministic fallback policy
Canary: deploy to 'hetero-gpu-canary' with a 5% traffic weight and run baseline + stress benchmarks
Rollout: ramp to 25% -> 50% -> full with rollback gates on latency/regression alerts
qa_steps: Run prelink verifier across the existing GPU artifact matrix and capture diffs
Execute canary perf harness comparing master vs sandbox branch under identical load
Inject mismatched CUTLASS/Triton pairs and assert error codes and no late symbol resolution
Run memory-pressure tests to ensure sandbox does not increase resident set significantly
Smoke test RPC pathing and model warmup hooks after the sandboxed initialization
risks: Sandbox FD-passing complexity could break on certain distros (musl/static) unless we add compatibility shims
Collision with other runtime processes that rely on non-documented symbols may surface as hard failures
Perf regressions if sandbox prelinking serializes startup too aggressively — needs async warmup tuning
Edge-case kernels that use nonstandard symbol versions may require temporary whitelist exceptions
notes: We will keep an opt-out feature flag for Dedicated clusters during initial rollout. Coordinate with Platform/DevExp to add flags and Telemetry to Console so customers can see prelink validation status per node.
